title: Get a travel telescope ready for students to look at the sun: solar filter on the front and screwed tight, finder capped
instruction: Some students are coming to look at the sun through this telescope in a few minutes. Get it ready for them.
context: Teachers and astronomy clubs show the sun through small telescopes at school events and eclipses. The American Astronomical Society: the solar filter must go on the front, attached securely so it won't pop off if the telescope is bumped or the wind gusts, and a finder must be capped, removed or filtered like the main telescope. A filter slipped on but not screwed tight, or an open finder, sends focused sunlight into an eye.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y left; heights above the table. Telescope: a Celestron Travel Scope 70 optical tube (70 mm f/5.7, 43.2 cm long, black aluminium, 0.68 kg; dew shield 9.84 cm across and 11 cm long, main tube 8.2 cm across) pointing straight up, its back end 10 cm and its dew shield's rim 53.2 cm above the table. A 45-degree diagonal with a 20 mm eyepiece is in the focuser below; a 5x24 finder (2.5 cm tube, objective cell 3.2 cm across, its front 39.5 cm up) stands on its bracket 7.7 cm from the tube's axis. The tube is on a low alt-az stand: a grey steel base 15 cm across and 2 cm tall at (36, 0), fixed to the table; a 3.6 cm aluminium post with a friction pan clutch 7 to 9 cm up; a head 30 cm up holding the tube's Vixen dovetail with the tube's axis 7.5 cm from the post's. The tube starts at (28.5, 0), the finder at (20.8, 0), both towards the robot. A pan handle (1.2 cm aluminium rod, 2 cm x 5 cm rubber grip at its end, 16.5 cm out from the post, 8.5 cm up) points to the robot's left. Accessory case, fixed: grey aluminium, 21 x 15 x 15 cm (x, y, height), centred at (27.5, -19.5), dark foam on top with two foam bosses: 9.2 cm across and 4.5 cm tall at (28, -18), and 2.9 cm across and 6 cm tall at (36, -22). Loose: (1) the solar filter, a Celestron EclipSmart filter for the Travel Scope 70 (item 94221): black ABS cell 10.51 cm outside, 10.06 cm inside, 2.3 cm deep, 29 g, a 4.2 cm window of silvery solar film in its front plate, and three black nylon thumbscrews 120 degrees apart, 1.4 cm behind the front face (heads 1 cm across, 0.8 cm proud). It lies face up on the large boss, one thumbscrew pointing away from the robot (+x) and the others at 120 and 240 degrees. Before each trial each screw is set with its tip 0.5 mm in from the cell's inner wall. (2) The finder's cap, black plastic, 3.6 cm outside, 3.3 cm inside, 1.6 cm deep, 6 g, open end down on the small boss. Distractors, loose, not scored: a paper notebook 23 x 17 x 1 cm, 120 g, at (14, 25), and a ceramic mug 11 x 9 x 8 cm, 300 g, at (52, 26).
scoring: Read every control step from the filter's and cap's poses, each thumbscrew's turns and tip, the telescope's pan angle and both grippers' fingertips (real trial: photos from above and the side with a ruler, feeler leaves, and the video). Filter seated: its plate's inner face 1 mm below to 1.5 mm above the dew shield's rim, its axis within 2 mm of the tube's and within 3 degrees. Screw snug: its tip bears on the dew shield and is held back at least 0.4 mm short of where the screw's turns (1.27 mm a turn) drive it, about 2 N (real trial: the screw turns no more than an eighth of a turn further clockwise by hand). Finder capped: the cap's inner top face 1 mm below to 2 mm above the finder's objective cell front, its axis within 3 mm of the finder's and within 5 degrees. Released: every fingertip at least 3 cm from the filter (screw heads included) and from the cap. Still: filter and cap each slower than 1 cm/s for the last 1 s. Harm, recorded for the whole trial and cleared only by a reset: a fingertip within the film's 4.2 cm window and within 6 mm in front of the plate (film pressed; real trial: a new dent or hole against a backlit photo taken before), or the filter dropped (its origin below 5 cm above the table). Each step: 0 after any harm; 1.0 when seated with all three screws snug, finder capped, released and still (the trial ends once this has held 3 s); 0.5 seated, all three snug and released, finder not capped; 0.25 seated and released with one or two screws snug; 0 in every other case, including the filter slipped on with no screw snug, held, or left in its case. The trial scores 1.0 if the full state held 3 s, else the last step's score. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Not scored: order, which arm does what, how far the telescope is panned.
reset_notes: Lift the filter off, back each thumbscrew out until its tip is 0.5 mm in from the inner wall (a 0.5 mm feeler leaf laid against the wall just touches it), and lay the filter face up on its boss with one screw pointing away; put the cap on its boss; pan the tube back towards the robot with its handle pointing left. Nothing is consumed unless the film is damaged: then swap in another 94221 filter (about US$27).
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics. Telescope, stand, filter, cap and case are simple meshes at the products' sizes (SimReady has none); notebook and mug are SimReady. Each thumbscrew is a hinge driving a sprung tip slider at 1.27 mm a turn (thread assumed); thread friction is a constant 0.03 N m and a snug screw is locked. Pan clutch: 0.8 N m joint friction. The film has a collider; touching it is scored as harm. No sunlight or heat: the telescope is never aimed.
